description:
The Back-To-Lab Post-Doctoral Fellowship Programme is an initiative launched by the Department of Science and Technology in India. 

This programme was officially launched in 2020. 

The primary objective of this fellowship is to encourage Indian researchers who have completed their doctoral studies to return to India and contribute to the scientific community. 

The programme aims to enhance the research capabilities in the country by providing support to post-doctoral researchers. 

The initiative specifically targets Indian nationals who have pursued their Ph.D. abroad. 

The fellowship is designed to provide a conducive environment for these researchers to engage in high-quality research in Indian institutions. 

The programme has set a measurable target of facilitating the return of at least 500 researchers over the next five years. 

The fellowship offers a financial support of INR 55,000 per month. 

In addition to the monthly stipend, the fellowship also provides a research grant of up to INR 5 lakhs. 

This research grant can be utilized for various research-related expenses such as equipment, materials, and travel for research purposes. 

The duration of the fellowship is typically for a period of two years. 

However, it can be extended for an additional year based on the performance of the fellow and the approval of the concerned authorities. 

Eligibility for the Back-To-Lab Post-Doctoral Fellowship Programme is specifically defined. 

Applicants must be Indian nationals who have completed their Ph.D. from a recognized institution outside India. 

There is no upper age limit specified for applicants. 

However, applicants must have completed their Ph.D. within the last five years to be eligible. 

The application process for the fellowship is straightforward and involves several steps. 

Interested candidates must first visit the official website of the Department of Science and Technology. 

They need to fill out the online application form available on the website. 

The application form requires candidates to provide details about their educational qualifications and research experience. 

Candidates must also submit a research proposal outlining their intended research work in India. 

In addition to the proposal, applicants need to provide a copy of their Ph.D. degree certificate. 

They must also submit a detailed curriculum vitae highlighting their academic and research achievements. 

Two recommendation letters from recognized experts in the field are also required. 

Once the application is submitted, it undergoes a rigorous review process. 

The review committee evaluates the applications based on the quality of the research proposal and the applicant's credentials. 

Shortlisted candidates are then invited for an interview. 

The final selection is based on the performance during the interview and the overall application. 

The fellowship is disbursed on a monthly basis. 

The first installment is typically released after the candidate has joined the host institution in India. 

Subsequent payments are made at the beginning of each month. 

The research grant is released in phases based on the research requirements and progress. 

The implementing authority for this fellowship programme is the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India. 

The department is responsible for overseeing the entire process, from application to disbursement of funds. 

For any inquiries or assistance, candidates can contact the Department of Science and Technology through their official email or helpline. 

The programme aims to strengthen the research ecosystem in India by attracting talent from abroad. 

It is expected to foster collaborations between Indian institutions and international research communities. 

The initiative aligns with the broader goals of the Indian government to promote scientific research and innovation. 

The Back-To-Lab Post-Doctoral Fellowship Programme is part of a larger strategy to enhance India's position in the global research landscape. 

By providing financial support and resources, the programme aims to facilitate cutting-edge research in various fields. 

This includes areas such as biotechnology, information technology, environmental science, and health sciences. 

The programme also encourages interdisciplinary research, allowing fellows to collaborate across different scientific domains. 

The initiative has received positive feedback from the academic community. 

Many researchers have expressed their appreciation for the support provided through this fellowship. 

The programme is seen as a significant step towards reversing the brain drain phenomenon. 

It aims to create an environment where Indian researchers can thrive and contribute to national development. 

The fellowship also emphasizes the importance of mentorship. 

Fellows are encouraged to engage with senior researchers and faculty members at their host institutions. 

This mentorship is intended to enhance the research capabilities of the fellows and facilitate knowledge transfer. 

The programme has a dedicated monitoring mechanism to assess the progress of the fellows. 

Regular reports are required from the fellows to ensure accountability and track research outcomes. 

The Back-To-Lab Post-Doctoral Fellowship Programme is expected to have a lasting impact on India's research landscape. 

It aims to build a robust network of researchers who can contribute to solving pressing societal challenges. 

The initiative is part of the government's commitment to invest in human capital and scientific research. 

In conclusion, the Back-To-Lab Post-Doctoral Fellowship Programme represents a strategic effort by the Indian government to attract talented researchers back to the country. 

Through financial support and a structured framework, the programme aims to enhance India's research capabilities and foster innovation. 

The initiative not only benefits the fellows but also contributes to the overall advancement of science and technology in India.
